narrative.overview:
Checkmate keeps the colours of a mahogany-and-brass games cabinet and drops its period costume. Every surface is a flat, softly rounded slab of one colour with a hairline edge and a soft shadow falling from above; there are no textures, rivets, bevels, engraving or serif faces. What survives of the machine is behavioural rather than decorative: counters that roll, a gauge needle that settles, a gear that turns per correct move, a bell that swings and one stamp that lands when a puzzle is solved.

The page is dark (mahogany) with two light materials laid on it: parchment for anything you read (the Daily problem, puzzle cards, the solved slip) and brass for the board's frame and the one primary action. Density is moderate: a board-first layout with a single side column, generous 44px controls, and short copy for casual players.

One grotesk does all the talking. Geist sets UI and display alike; Geist Mono appears only where a value is a code or a count.
keyCharacteristics: Dark mahogany ground; parchment for reading; brass for the board frame, selection and the primary action.
Flat single-colour surfaces, 16px corners, hairline inset border, soft drop shadow from above.
Geist everywhere, 700 at -0.02em for display; Geist Mono only for IDs, ratings and counters.
Every control is a real form control (radios, checkbox switch, native select, buttons) restyled.
Mechanical motion with a heavy ease-out; reduced motion makes every state instant.

rules.name: The One Meaning Rule
rules.body: Brass means "chosen or primary", verdigris means "correct" (and the keyboard's place on the board), oxblood means "wrong, in check, or stamped solved". Never use a signal colour as decoration.

rules.name: The One Stamp Rule
rules.body: The oxblood stamp appears once: on the solved slip. Solved status everywhere else is the quiet verdigris pill badge.

rules.name: The Board Woods Rule
rules.body: Maple and walnut belong to the 64 squares. No other surface uses them.

rules.name: The Mono Means Data Rule
rules.body: Geist Mono sets IDs, ratings and counters (and key names in instructions). Prose, headings and status messages are always Geist.

rules.name: The Weight Not Family Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy comes from weight (400 / 600 / 700) and size. Don't introduce a second display face.

rules.name: The Light From Above Rule
rules.body: Highlights sit on top edges, shadows fall below. Never light an element from the side or cast an offset shadow.

rules.name: The Flat Slab Rule
rules.body: A surface is one colour (brass may carry its gentle top-to-bottom sheen), a hairline, and a soft shadow. No textures, grain, rivets, screws, bevels or engraving.

dos: Do build every control from a native element (button, radio, checkbox switch, select) and restyle it; segmented controls are radio groups in a fieldset with a legend.
Do keep tap targets at least 2.75rem (44px) tall.
Do use brass for the selected or primary thing, verdigris for correct and for the board's keyboard focus, oxblood for error, check and the single SOLVED stamp.
Do set IDs, ratings and counters in Geist Mono with tabular figures; everything else in Geist, display at 700 / -0.02em.
Do separate surfaces with a colour step, a 1px hairline and a soft shadow falling from above.
Do keep reduced motion instant: transitions and animations collapse to 1ms with no delay, steam is hidden, and the stamp and bell keep their final poses.
Do pair colour with a second signal: difficulty pips carry the word, status lamps carry a text line.
donts: Don't add textures, wood grain, rivets, screws, bevels, engraving or embossed type to any surface.
Don't use a serif or slab display face, or a second display family.
Don't use mono for prose, headings or status messages.
Don't add a second stamp, or use oxblood for decoration; solved state elsewhere is the verdigris badge.
Don't use maple or walnut outside the board squares.
Don't cast hard or offset shadows; shadows are soft and fall straight down.
Don't use text glyphs or emoji as icons; icons are inline SVG.
